text:
maya: Quick q — PR #482 introduced a `cached_tokens` field on /v1/generate responses. I wanted to flag compatibility and billing questions before we roll it wide.

maya: Example we're returning now for a single call (simplified):
```json
{
  "id": "gen_abc123",
  "choices": [{ "text": "..." }],
  "usage": { "prompt_tokens": 120, "completion_tokens": 80, "cached_tokens": 50 }
}
```

maya: Questions: 1) any SDKs expecting a flat `tokens` field that will break? 2) should `cached_tokens` be included in the usage object for billing, or only in a separate `reconciliation` field? 3) streaming delta behavior — how do we report cached tokens incrementally?

ashwin: tagging infra/runtime — the SDKs we've maintained (js/py/go) don't look for a `tokens` top-level key; they parse `usage`. but some customers' older integrations do string-scraping logs for 'tokens:' which sucks. :grimacing:

ashwin: From a contract POV `usage` is the right place, but we should mark `cached_tokens` as optional and documented as "non-billable" by default until billing finishes the recon flow. Backward compat: treat missing `cached_tokens` as 0.

sophie: @maya @ashwin billing view: we cannot bill cached tokens as if they were produced tokens without reconciliation. Historically we bill on final non-cached delta. If runtime reports `cached_tokens` separately we can subtract them in the billing job. We need a clear flag: `cached_tokens` boolean or reason codes to explain why they were cached.

sophie: also need to confirm whether cached tokens are prefix cache hits (no infra cost) or KV-reuse (still had generation cost earlier). semantics matter for finance.

julian: runtime notes — `cached_tokens` currently counts tokens served from prefix/KV cache with no token-generation work on this request. so they should be non-billable for this request (we already charged when cache was populated). For streaming, we emit a running `usage` snapshot after the stream closes; streaming clients may see partial `usage` in events but we only guarantee the final `usage` object.

julian: Implementation detail: for streaming we don't send `usage` in every chunk. We append a final `:usage` meta frame when the stream finishes, e.g., `data: {"usage": {...}}` so SDK consumers know to read final. That avoids double-counting intermediate deltas.

maya: ok — sounds like defaults: `usage` includes prompt/completion/cached, `cached_tokens` optional, and final streaming frame contains authoritative usage. Can we standardize a small enum for cache reason? e.g., `cache_reason: ["prefix", "kv", "model_cached"]`

ashwin: I like the enum. Keep it optional string list: `cache_reasons: ["prefix"]` so future multi-source caches possible. Also add `billing_status` with values `"billable" | "non_billable" | "pending_recon"` — default `non_billable` for cached. That makes reconciliation deterministic.

sophie: Billing wants `billing_status`. For `pending_recon` we'll produce a reconciliation record with original request_id and tokens to either bill or credit. We also want `recon_id` in the response when pending so downstream pipelines can correlate.

billing-bot: INFO: created recon job template `recon/2026-03-cache-v1` — will listen for `billing_status==\"pending_recon\"` and `recon_id` to pick up adjustments.

infra-bot: deploy bot — rolled PR #482 to staging at 1773009900, canary 10%. No errors in canary logs so far.

maya: Action items: (1) Runtime: add `billing_status` and optional `cache_reasons` + `recon_id` when appropriate. (2) SDKs: tolerate missing `cached_tokens` and read `usage` from final stream frame or HTTP body. (3) Billing: implement recon pipeline that consumes `recon_id`.

ashwin: I'll open a small RFC doc with examples and a compatibility table. cc: @julian for exact semantics and @sophie for billing status states.

sophie: I can prototype the recon job next week. If we set `non_billable` default, finance won't see surprises.

julian: I'll change the streaming behavior to guarantee the final usage frame and include `recon_id` when `billing_status==\"pending_recon\"`. ETA EOW for staging update.

maya: perfect — thanks all. if anyone spots an integration that actually expects `tokens` top-level please ping me and we'll add a compatibility shim. :thumbsup:

ashwin: small note for release notes: mention "new optional usage fields: cached_tokens, cache_reasons, billing_status, recon_id" and that SDKs should only consume final usage data.

maya: closing loop — I'll wait for the RFC link and then mark this thread resolved.

julian: RFC at https://redwood.internal/rfc/482-cache-usage (staged).

maya: received, thanks!
